nodes.label: COVID-19 US-states bundle EDA
nodes.rationale: 49 nodes x 164 weeks, fully observed, standard fixed_50_20_30 and per_node_train scaler; the shortest development panel. M is all-ones by construction because absence before a state's first case is a genuine zero, not a missing observation, so COVID contributes no zero-fill covariate shift and the LOCF input fill is a no-op.

nodes.label: The Omicron peak lands inside the COVID validation fold
nodes.rationale: The national maximum (2022-01-15, 5.14M cases, 13.8x the median week) sits at val week 21 of 33, making the val mean 2.8x train and 2.8x test. Early stopping therefore selects on a once-in-the-panel event that never recurs in the scored period. The recommendation is still to keep fixed_50_20_30: protocol consistency across diseases is worth more than a better-conditioned COVID split, since moving the cut only for COVID would make its transfer cells incomparable to every other cell. An earlier 'train->test regime shift' note was wrong - the test/train national mean ratio is 1.03x; the shift is a spike inside val.

nodes.label: bias_c mean-vs-median count-space correction
nodes.rationale: Measures the gap between the count-space mean (what RMSE rewards) and the count-space median (what the quantile head predicts). COVID's node-median gap is 3.03x against influenza's 1.74x on the identical nodes, so COVID should fit a visibly larger bias_c - but it is fitted on val, which owns Omicron, so it will over-correct. This is the first bundle where the val-only fitting rule is actively harmful rather than merely conservative; the defensible alternative is fitting COVID's bias_c on train and saying so.

nodes.label: Node-level-mean variance diagnostic and the dengue discrepancy
nodes.rationale: COVID's cross-node level gradient (0.0090) is 7x flatter than influenza's on the same 49 nodes, so the spatial channel has even less to propagate. Two numbers are in circulation for dengue - 0.948 versus 0.0234 - and japan and us-states match exactly, so the method agrees everywhere except dengue; the likely cause is the denominator (a node mean over all T is crushed toward zero at 78 per cent exact zeros, a mean over observed cells only is not). Both are defensible, they are different statistics, and neither should be quoted until it is pinned down.

nodes.label: COVID vs influenza on the identical 49 nodes
nodes.rationale: This is the reason the bundle exists. The graph and covariates are bit-identical and the node ids are disjoint, while Spearman 0.695 on node totals means the two diseases rank the same states similarly but far from identically. A transfer result between these two bundles therefore isolates disease transfer from graph transfer, which no other cross-disease cell in the study can do.

nodes.label: encoder_mc arm matters most on COVID
nodes.rationale: COVID has the largest mean/median gap of any panel (3.03x), so the arm that corrects for it has the most to do here.
